messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [P1] High GPU queue growth in us-west-2-gpu-prod -> autoscales failing. Alerts: queue_length > 1200 for 6m, error-rate on driver pool rising. Paging oncall
amy_oncall: ack'ing, joining now. seeing high token queue on the dashboard.
amy_oncall: @raj_runtime can you confirm if this is runtime-level (OOM/Xid) or purely autoscaler backlog?
raj_runtime: seeing both. multiple nodes reporting CUDA/Xid resets + repeated OOM kills on worker processes. app-level requests pile up. sample from node-42 logs:```
[2026-03-15T02:12:11Z] gpu0: Xid 124: GPU fault, context lost
[2026-03-15T02:12:12Z] process pid=23845 killed by OOM killer
[2026-03-15T02:12:18Z] driver reset invoked
```
raj_runtime: driver resets drop effective capacity -> autoscaler tries to add nodes but scale requests are being rejected.
tomas_infra: pulling autoscaler logs now. hitting rate/quotas on pool allocation. excerpt:```
INFO 2026-03-15T02:10:55 scale_request: pool us-west-2-gpu-prod desired=+8 (current 12)
ERROR 2026-03-15T02:10:56 scale_request: rejected reason=quota_exceeded project_quota=20 current_alloc=20
```
tomas_infra: total GPU quota for this account bumped earlier for other customers, so autoscaler can't grow.
amy_oncall: ok — two failure modes: (1) nodes flapping/driver resets -> effective capacity drop, (2) autoscaler rejects new capacity due to quota -> queue grows and throttle triggers. we need parallel mitigations.
maya_sre: will start manual mitigations. prioritization: evict background/low-priority requests, enable model-fallback to smaller quantized variant, and attempt emergency quota bump with cloud account.
leo_product: tagging impacted customers - high-volume inference customers A and B seeing elevated 5xx and latency. @sarah_cs please start impact comms with initial ETA note.
sarah_cs: on it — sending heads-up to A + B; will tell them we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA timeline.
raj_runtime: quick commands I'm running:```
# show nodes with Xid/errors
rgpuctl nodes --pool us-west-2-gpu-prod --filter "last_xid>0" --json | jq '.[] | {name, last_xid, last_reset}'
# restart driver on one node (testing)
ssh root@node-42 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service && sudo nvidia-smi -q'
```
raj_runtime: restarting driver on node-42 reduced local Xid churn, but there are several nodes with repeated resets. suspect kernel-driver mismatch on a subset from last rollout.
tomas_infra: escalated to cloud quota team for emergency bump. also spinning up spare nodes from a different quota pool (us-west-2-gpu-burst) — will attach to us-west-2-gpu-prod if approved.
deploy-bot: deployment event: gpu-driver/2026-03-14T23:50 -> rolled to 60% of fleet. Can confirm nodes updated since then.
raj_runtime: that 60% rollout timing aligns with when errors started. possible bad driver patch.
amy_oncall: action list now: 1) abort further driver rollouts; 2) rollback driver to known-good on remaining nodes (tomas to coordinate); 3) manual cluster scale-up from burst pool if quota bump granted; 4) evict low-priority jobs and enable fallback model route (maya); 5) restart drivers on flapping nodes (raj).
maya_sre: running eviction script now to drain batch jobs from prod queue:```
./scripts/evict-low-priority.sh --pool us-west-2-gpu-prod --threshold 500
```
maya_sre: also flipping feature-flag to route new requests to quantized-llama-q4 on overflow. hitting the flag now.
leo_product: please record any customer-facing latency/5xx numbers so we can quantify impact for the postmortem.
sarah_cs: relayed initial notice to Customer A: "We're experiencing elevated latency and transient errors on GPU endpoints. Our on-call is actively mitigating; next update in 30m or sooner."
amy_oncall: autoscaler workaround: tomas, can you manually create a smaller node from burst pool and attach it to DFS so we don't wait for quota team? even temporary helps.
tomas_infra: creating node from us-west-2-gpu-burst now. running attach script.```
infractl allocate --pool us-west-2-gpu-burst --count 2 --type gpu-a100xlarge --attach-to us-west-2-gpu-prod
```
tomas_infra: attach succeeded for 1/2, second node failed due to soft quota check but we'll try again.
raj_runtime: after adding one burst node, queue length dropped ~12% and p95 latency improved 18%. still seeing occasional Xid spikes.
amy_oncall: good. keep driver restarts and rollback plan. raj, can you confirm which driver build to roll back to (hash)?
raj_runtime: rolling back to driver-510.72 which was stable last week. preparing rollback playbook.
maya_sre: feature-flag routed ~45% of overflow to quantized model; overall token cost lower, latency slightly higher but acceptable.
leo_product: customers A/B still seeing reduced errors; need to quantify reduction. can someone post dashboards?
maya_sre: screenshot uploaded to thread (link) — queue trending down.
sarah_cs: Customer A responded: thanks for the update, wants ETA for full restoration. asked if we can prioritize their traffic.
amy_oncall: we should avoid per-customer exceptions; rely on fallback and manual scale.
amy_oncall: preparing oncall handoff note: I'll be oncall for another 25m, then handing to @maya_sre. leaving summary and open items.
amy_oncall: SUMMARY (for handoff) -> root cause suspected: bad driver rollout + quota limits prevented autoscaler recovery => queue surge and throttling; mitigation in progress: rollback driver, manual burst nodes attached, evict low-priority jobs, route overflow to quantized model, emergency quota request pending.
amy_oncall: OPEN ACTIONS -> (raj) finish driver rollback on remaining nodes; (tomas) continue to attach burst nodes / chase quota; (maya) monitor fallback errors and manage routing; (sarah) customer comms; (leo) track impacted customers list.
maya_sre: ack'ing handoff. I'll take post-oncall ownership after amy. will post an update every 30m or on any customer-impact change.
amy_oncall: handing over to @maya_sre in 5m. logging final note and brief timeline for postmortem. :thumbsup:
maya_sre: taking over. thanks all.
